categories.name: SQL Injection
categories.summary: User input is glued into a SQL string, so the input can change the query itself.

categories.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
categories.summary: User input is written into a page without encoding, so a browser runs it as markup or script.

categories.name: Broken Access Control / IDOR
categories.summary: The server trusts an ID from the request and never checks the record belongs to the caller.

categories.name: Hardcoded Secret
categories.summary: A key, token or password sits in source code, where everyone with repo access can read it.

categories.name: Weak Password Hashing
categories.summary: Passwords are stored with a fast, unsalted hash that attackers can crack at huge speed.

categories.name: Path Traversal
categories.summary: A file path built from user input can climb out of the intended folder with ../ sequences.

categories.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
categories.summary: The server fetches any URL a user supplies, including internal services and cloud metadata.

categories.name: Insecure Deserialisation
categories.owasp: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures
categories.summary: Untrusted bytes are turned back into live objects, which can run attacker-chosen code.

categories.name: Missing Input Validation
categories.summary: A value is used without checking its range, type or format, so business rules can be broken.

categories.name: Verbose Error Messages
categories.summary: Errors return stack traces, queries or internals that map the system for an attacker.

categories.name: Insecure Data Storage
categories.summary: Sensitive data is saved on the phone in plain files or shared storage that other apps, backups or a rooted phone can read.

categories.name: Insecure Communication (TLS)
categories.summary: The app accepts certificates it shouldn't, so someone on the same network can read and change its traffic.

categories.name: Sensitive Data in Logs
categories.summary: PINs, tokens or personal data are written to logs or crash reports that other people and tools can read.

categories.name: Unsafe WebView
categories.summary: A WebView with JavaScript and an app bridge can be pointed at pages the app doesn't control.

categories.name: Exposed App Component
categories.summary: An activity, receiver or provider is open to every other app on the phone, skipping the app's own checks.

categories.name: Permissive Data Rules
categories.summary: Database or storage rules let people read or change data that isn't theirs.

categories.name: Secret Exposed in Build or Deploy
categories.summary: A key or password ends up in an image, artifact or file that far more people can reach than should.

categories.name: Untrusted Pipeline Code
categories.summary: The build runs code from somewhere you don't control, with your secrets and permissions.

categories.name: Excessive Privileges
categories.summary: A container or service account gets far more power than its job needs, so one bug becomes a takeover.

categories.name: Exposed Files or Backups
categories.summary: The web server hands out files that were never meant to be public: backups, .env files, source code.
